Chapter 30: Zero-Glue C/C++ Interoperability & Native Math

A major barrier when adopting new systems programming languages is the "glue code problem": writing thousands of lines of wrappers, FFI bindings, Cython definitions, or PyO3 adapters to call existing C/C++ libraries.

Cluster-lang solves this completely with Zero-Glue C Integration. You can directly include C standard library headers, link system shared libraries, and call native C functions with zero overhead and zero wrappers.

This chapter covers:

1. The c_include Directive for instant standard header ingestion.

2. The link Directive & Compiler Linker Flags (-l, -L

).

3. The extern fn Declaration for custom C/C++ symbol signatures.

4. Native Double & Floating-Point LLVM Lowering.

5. High-Performance Built-in Math Functions.

1. Direct Header Ingestion with c_include

To use standard C functions, simply include the header at the top of your Cluster source file:

c_include "math.h"
c_include "stdio.h"

fn main():
    # Call C standard library functions directly!
    x := 16.0
    s := sqrt(x)
    put "Square root of 16.0 is: " + to_text(s)
    
    val := cos(0.0)
    put "Cos(0.0) is: " + to_text(val)

The compiler automatically imports function prototypes, return types, and parameter signatures for headers like math.h, stdio.h, stdlib.h, string.h, time.h, and unistd.h.

2. Dynamic Library Linking (link)

When your code depends on external C libraries (such as libm, libcrypto, libcurl, or libsqlite3), use the link directive:

# Instructs the linker to link libm (-lm)
link "m"

# Instructs the linker to link libssl (-lssl)
link "ssl"

You can also pass library names and library search paths directly from the CLI:

./cl run -lm -L/usr/local/lib main.cl

The Cluster compiler automatically injects -Wl,-rpath flags to ensure your compiled binaries locate shared libraries at runtime without manual LD_LIBRARY_PATH configuration.

3. External Function Declarations (extern fn)

For custom third-party C/C++ libraries that do not have automated header mappings, you can declare external functions using the extern fn syntax:

link "m"

# Declare external C signatures
extern fn hypot(x: float, y: float) -> float
extern fn pow(base: float, exponent: float) -> float

fn main():
    h := hypot(3.0, 4.0)
    put "Hypotenuse (3, 4) = " + to_text(h)    # 5.000000

    p := pow(2.0, 10.0)
    put "2^10 = " + to_text(p)                 # 1024.000000

4. Native 64-bit Float Lowering

Cluster-lang features full native LLVM double lowering for IEEE 754 64-bit floating point numbers:

  • Float Arithmetic: Lowered to native CPU instructions (fadd, fsub, fmul, fdiv, fneg).
  • Float Comparisons: Evaluated via IEEE compliant ordered comparison (fcmp oeq, fcmp one, fcmp olt, fcmp ogt).
  • Automatic Int-to-Float Promotion: Passing integer values where floats are expected automatically inserts zero-cost sitofp conversions.
fn main():
    a := 3.14159
    b := 2.71828

    sum := a + b
    diff := a - b
    prod := a * b
    div := a / b

    put sum
    put diff
    put prod
    put div
